weights._note: Bengaluru's V0 scoring leans on named-kere prominence + historical disappearance rather than the Chennai-style 6-factor model (size, lost-proximity, river-pollution, industrial-proximity, type-bonus, census-condition). The Bengaluru data layer we ship doesn't yet support census-condition (no point-in-polygon spatial join) or river-pollution overlay - so the V0 algorithm is intentionally narrative-and-status-led. Will refine when KSPCB lake WQ + restoration-projects data lands.

notes: Scored bodies are a curated set of 17 named kere across BBMP/GBA. Fully-lost bodies (Dharmambudhi, Sampangi, Karanji Anjaneya, Akkithimmanahalli, Domlur) carry osm_id=null because the original tank is now a built-over surface; the score still surfaces them as 'historical priority' on the restoration view. Bellandur carries the highest narrative_bonus because the foam-fire chronology is the city's flagship water story (Forward Foundation v Karnataka, NGT 2018, Rs 500 cr order). Hesaraghatta + TG Halli get an Arkavati-system bonus reflecting BWSSB's IPR pilot.

water_bodies.name: Bellandur Lake
water_bodies.rationale: severely reduced · foam-and-fire flagship (May 2015, Feb 2018, 2021) · Forward Foundation v Karnataka NGT case anchor · largest kere in BBMP · receives ~400-500 MLD untreated K&C valley sewage

water_bodies.name: Varthur Lake
water_bodies.rationale: severely reduced · downstream of Bellandur · receives the same K&C valley load · second-largest BBMP kere · 2017 fire incident

water_bodies.name: Dharmambudhi
water_bodies.rationale: fully lost · Kempegowda's second-built kere (mid-16th c.) · drained 1950s for Kempegowda Bus Station / Majestic · the bus stand bears the founder's name but the water does not

water_bodies.name: Hesaraghatta Lake
water_bodies.rationale: severely reduced · BWSSB's 1894 first piped-supply source (K. Seshadri Iyer, Diwan of Mysore) · Arkavati impoundment · catchment built over · still the largest kere by area in the region

water_bodies.name: Sampangi tank
water_bodies.rationale: fully lost · 16th c. Kempegowda-era kere · drained for Sri Kanteerava Stadium + hockey complex · gave its name to Sampangi Tank Road

water_bodies.name: TG Halli / Chamaraja Sagara
water_bodies.rationale: defunct · BWSSB's 1933 second piped-supply impoundment · upstream catchment lost to urbanisation · being repurposed as BWSSB-SUEZ 110 MLD IPR (indirect potable reuse) pilot · India's largest of its kind

water_bodies.name: Madiwala Lake
water_bodies.rationale: functional but stressed · upstream of Hosur Road · BBMP Lake Conservation Authority manages · regular fish-kill events

water_bodies.name: Halasuru (Ulsoor) Lake
water_bodies.rationale: severely reduced from pre-Cantonment extent · 1811 British 50K-troop garrison was laid out around this lake · subsequent road + rail encroachment cut the perimeter · symbol of the Cantonment/Pete water-access split

water_bodies.name: Hebbal Lake
water_bodies.rationale: functional · IISc Groundwater Outlook 2025 names Hebbal among 65 critically over-extracted wards · 60 MLD Hebbal STP discharges here · DBOT tertiary plant supplies treated water to nearby industries

water_bodies.name: Jakkur Lake
water_bodies.rationale: restored exemplar · Jakkur Lake + STP wetland-treatment integration is a model BWSSB project · 10 MLD STP feeding constructed wetland before discharge to lake · cited in IISc studies

water_bodies.name: Karanji Anjaneya tank
water_bodies.rationale: fully lost · tank bed redeveloped into Bishop Cotton Boys School playing fields + Richmond Road education campus

water_bodies.name: Akkithimmanahalli tank
water_bodies.rationale: fully lost · converted into Akkithimmanahalli Hockey Stadium in central Bengaluru · stadium keeps the kere's name; the water does not

water_bodies.name: Agara Lake
water_bodies.rationale: stressed · D'Souza & Nagendra 2011 Environmental Management paper documents the community-managed-commons -> state-managed-amenity transition; the most-studied single Bengaluru kere

water_bodies.name: Sankey Tank
water_bodies.rationale: amenity-restored · designed by Col Richard Hieram Sankey (British military engineer) in 1882 · cascade connections gone · survives as a decorative water body in central Malleshwaram

water_bodies.name: Yelahanka Lake
water_bodies.rationale: stressed · Yelahanka is named in IISc Groundwater Outlook 65-stress-ward list · serves the seat of Kempegowda's original Yelahanka Nadu chieftaincy

water_bodies.name: Lalbagh Tank
water_bodies.rationale: amenity · inside Lalbagh Botanical Garden (Hyder Ali / Tipu Sultan founded; 18th c.) · CGWB station ground · maintained as decorative water

water_bodies.name: Domlur tank
water_bodies.rationale: fully lost · drained for BDA Domlur Layout + arterial road network east of MG Road
